Mountain Base Instructions

Nightmare Before Christmas scene · version 3

Mountain base

The whole 64 × 32 layout as two modules that lift apart: Section A on the left, Section B on the right, each on four white 16 × 16 plates. Layout by Grok, built from its combined_v3 file. Each numbered step is one brick-height band, split into sub-steps of up to 14 pieces; 385 sub-steps in all.

Red boxWhere this sub-step's pieces go. New pieces are in full colour; everything built earlier is pale blue-grey.
Lime = any colourHidden inside the mountain. Use any spare pieces of that size; there are 650 of them.
CoordinatesSeen from the front: col counts studs from the left edge of the section (1–32), row counts from the front edge (1–32). A range like col 5-8 is the piece's full length.
Steep slopes"Slopes down to the front" means the low edge faces you. The 65°, 75° and double slopes are drawn with simplified shapes; go by the part number.
Tick listsTap a row when the piece is on. Ticks are saved in this browser.
col 1 ............................ col 32 row 32 ┌────────────────────────────────────┐ back (wall side) │ │ │ │ row 1 └────────────────────────────────────┘ front (viewer)
Where things goSection ASection BAfter the build

Where things go

Top-down, front at the bottom. Darker means taller. The dashed red line is the split between the two modules.

  1. Spiral Hill on Section A's plateau, back left.
  2. Jack's house on the flat snow in front of the ridge, a little right of centre so the peaks frame it.
  3. Oogie Boogie in the front-right corner, turned slightly toward the sleigh and the house, as if he's watching them.
  4. Christmas tree behind Oogie on the right side, just in front of the ridge, so it sits right of the house.
  5. Sleigh coming off the front of the foothills, angled toward the front centre, with the stags on their clear stands out over the flat snow. Keep it low and left of the house.

Left module · spiral plateau and foothills

Section A

23 steps · 185 sub-steps · 1684 pieces

The left 32 × 32 module. The back half rises as a solid block to a flat studs-up plateau 8 bricks high, where the set's Spiral Hill sits. The front half is snowy rock foothills, which the sleigh launches from. A few peaks at the right edge start the back ridge.

Right module · the back ridge

Section B

26 steps · 200 sub-steps · 1319 pieces

The right 32 × 32 module. A wall of steep peaks runs along the back, up to 25 bricks tall; the front is flat snow for Jack's house and the Christmas tree. The peaks are built from steep 65° and 75° slopes on hidden cores, so the upper sub-steps are small and fiddly; take them one at a time.

After the build

  1. Push the two modules together along the dashed line. Nothing crosses the join, so they can be split again to move them.
  2. Set the set's Spiral Hill on Section A's plateau; its base presses onto the studs.
  3. Place Jack's house, the tree and the sleigh as shown in Where things go.
  4. Scatter any spare white cheese slopes, round plates and tiles over the flat snow and the lower ledges.
